name: Foundation Base64 (swift-foundation 2025 rewrite)
baseline: Foundation base64EncodedString / Data(base64Encoded:) as shipped before February 2025
verdict_reason: Benchmarks posted on the merged swift-foundation PRs show 1 MB encodes 5.8-7x faster and 1 MB decodes 5.2-7.5x faster than the Foundation of the time, and later follow-ups report another 3-4x on encoding and about 2x on decoding. Rejecting invalid input got slower.
tier_reason: Measured by the change's author with swift-foundation's benchmark target, but the 2025 posts give no hardware or toolchain.
claimed_speedup: 1MB encode to String 414μs vs 2915μs (7x), to Data 494μs vs 2894μs (5.8x); JWT-header encode 120ns vs 409ns (3.4x); 1MB decode from String 405μs vs 3038μs (7.5x), from Data 406μs vs 2123μs (5.2x); invalid input after 257 bytes 2675ns vs 748ns (3.5x slower). Follow-ups: encoding '3-4 times' faster again, decoding 'Generally ~2, but up to 4 times' faster.
workload: swift-foundation Base64 benchmarks: encoding and decoding 1 MB buffers to and from String and Data, line-length options, a JWT header, and an invalid-input case
hardware: Not stated for the 2025 numbers; the follow-up PRs list Apple M1 and M6 machines
platforms: Foundation releases built from swift-foundation after February 2025 (first OS release not stated in the sources)
one_liner: Foundation's own Base64, rewritten in Swift in 2025: 1 MB encodes and decodes 5-7.5x faster than the version it replaced.
how_it_is_fast: A Swift encoder and decoder built on precomputed lookup tables (the swift-extras-base64 approach, contributed by the same author) write straight into the output buffer instead of going through the older implementation. The follow-up PRs restructure the loops so the compiler can auto-vectorize them and use Span for input and output.
use_it_when: Default choice for Base64 once your OS or toolchain includes the rewrite
Large payloads (images, attachments, JWT bodies) encoded or decoded in bulk
skip_it_when: Older OS versions without the change keep the old speed
Workloads dominated by rejecting malformed input: that path measured 3.5x slower
caveats: Author-measured; the 2025 posts give no hardware or toolchain.
Which OS release first ships each change is not stated; the October 2026 follow-ups are on main and probably not in a shipping OS yet.
'Baseline (in Foundation today)' is the system Foundation the author measured against in February 2025.
tradeoffs: Invalid-input rejection is slower than before (2675ns vs 748ns in the decode PR's measurement)

evidence.quote: The Base64 encoding logic can be made 3-4 times more performant.
Generally ~2, but up to 4 times faster decoding for large inputs, per benchmarks.
